hook.text: Purdue Pharma told doctors OxyContin was safe and rarely addictive. Over 500,000 Americans died.

buildup.text: Aggressive marketing pushed opioids for minor pain. Sales reps downplayed addiction risks to physicians.

discovery.text: Internal documents showed Purdue knew OxyContin was highly addictive years before admitting it publicly.

twist.text: The Sackler family earned $12 billion from OxyContin while communities were devastated by addiction.

climax.text: Half a million deaths. One company's compliance failure created a national health catastrophe.

punchline.text: Safe and non-addictive, they said. 500,000 died.

quiz.question: What did Purdue Pharma falsely claim about OxyContin?
options: That it was safe and rarely addictive
That it had no side effects at all
